title: A Behavioural Framework for Predicting and Understanding Loss of Control in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Systems
abstract: arXiv:2611.07953v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Frontier artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly operating over longer horizons with diminishing human oversight, raising the risk of loss of control: systems acting beyond effective human control with potentially irreversible consequences. Because such failures may become observable only after containment is difficult, they must be assessed prospectively. We introduce a behavioural framework that decomposes loss-of-control risk into three factors: misaligned motive, harm-enabling capability, and monitoring evasion. We operationalise these factors through 13 measurable aspects and 29 evaluation tasks, whose scores are combined into a single loss-of-control (LoC) score. Across 13 frontier models, the LoC score shows strong prospective validity, correlating with failure rates in contained long-horizon risk scenarios (Pearson r = 0.84). translated_title: 一个用于预测和理解前沿人工智能系统失控的行为框架
translated_abstract: 前沿人工智能系统越来越多地在更长的时间跨度上运行，而人类监督却在逐渐减少，这带来了失控的风险：即系统采取超出人类有效控制的行为，并可能造成不可逆转的后果。由于此类故障可能只有在难以遏制时才会显现出来，因此必须对其进行前瞻性评估。我们提出了一个行为框架，将失控风险分解为三个因素：动机错位、促成危害的能力以及规避监控。我们通过13个可测量的方面和29个评估任务对这些因素进行操作化，其得分被综合为一个单一的失控（LoC）评分。在13个前沿模型上，失控评分表现出很强的前瞻有效性，与受控长时程风险场景中的失败率相关（Pearson r = 0.84）。风险在各模型间呈现系统性变化，且无法仅用能力来解释。
tldr: 本文提出一个行为框架，将前沿AI系统的失控风险分解为动机错位、危害促成能力和监控规避三个因素，并验证了其失控评分在13个前沿模型上对实际失败率的前瞻预测能力（Pearson r = 0.84），且表明风险无法仅由模型能力解释。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a behavioural framework that decomposes loss-of-control risk in frontier AI systems into misaligned motive, harm-enabling capability, and monitoring evasion, with a validated LoC score (Pearson r = 0.84) that prospectively predicts failure rates across 13 frontier models beyond what capability alone can explain.
